meta.intro: Today's throughline: the cost of running agents is falling while the physical limits of power, skilled labour and fab capacity keep tightening.
meta.briefingTitle: GPT-6.1 Terra Halves Agent Costs, Amazon's GPUs Wait for Power, and Japan's Kumamoto 3nm Arrives Small
meta.summary: Software is getting cheaper to run while the physical world sets the pace. OpenAI's Terra cuts agent prices to $1/$5 per million tokens, yet Amazon reportedly holds about $5B of GB300 racks it cannot power. Capital is moving to physical-world retrofits and agent auditing at seed. In Japan, METI's 3nm approval for TSMC Kumamoto comes with a fraction of planned volume, and a government LLM bake-off may decide domestic models.

gaps.label: Sovereign frontier-model pretraining
gaps.note: Unchanged — Gennai is testing 32B-class domestic models against foreign ones, while open Chinese and US weights (Kimi, Muse Spark Open) arrive at frontier scale.

gaps.label: Depth of private risk capital for AI infrastructure
gaps.note: Unchanged — Bedrock's $600M and Tenstorrent's $1.5B in one week versus Japan's H1 growth of about 2% ex-Sakana and a ¥1.27B chip round.

gaps.label: Domestic leading-edge chip manufacturing
gaps.note: Up 1 — METI cleared TSMC Kumamoto 3nm, but at 6,000 wafers/month and Dec 2028, with Rapidus still lacking a named 2nm customer.

gaps.label: Early-stage AI venture formation
gaps.note: Unchanged — Japan's seed AI median (¥160M) shows no AI premium; US seeds like Asymptote's $5.5M target new categories such as agent auditing.

items.headline: OpenAI Ships GPT-6.1 Terra at $1/$5 per Million Tokens, Half of Sol's Price, Aimed at Cheap Computer-Use Agents
items.dek: A mid-tier model targets the volume end of agent work, and Artificial Analysis reports a big drop in confident guessing.

analysis.happening: Terra is live in ChatGPT, Codex and the API: $1 input, $0.05 cached, $5 output per million tokens, ~1.05M context. Artificial Analysis puts it 4 points below Sol and says it guesses 38% of the time when unsure, versus 88% for GPT-5.6 Terra.
analysis.now: Cost per computer-use task decides which always-on agents are affordable. Caveats: the 3x speed claim is OpenAI's own timing, and Terra trails Sol on coding and Terminal-Bench.
analysis.future: Watch whether Anthropic and Google answer with cheaper tiers, and for two weeks of real-world computer-use reliability reports.

items.headline: Bedrock Robotics Raises $600M at $4.1B for Retrofit Self-Driving Excavators, Eight Months After a $1.75B Valuation
items.dek: CapitalG and Emergence co-lead a kit-not-new-machine bet on construction's operator shortage.

analysis.happening: Bedrock's $600M Series C is co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital; Bessemer, Temasek and USIT are new, while 8VC, Valor, Georgian and Nvidia return. Nearly $1B raised since 2024. Excavators moved from pilots to commercial sites about two months ago.
analysis.now: The thesis is retrofit: sell a kit to existing fleets facing a skilled-operator shortage. Caveat: revenue is undisclosed and a few live sites are thin support for a $4.1B mark.
analysis.future: Watch revenue per machine and kit attach rates. Retrofit autonomy for mining, farming and Japan's ageing operator base is open ground.

items.headline: Amazon Is Reportedly Warehousing About $5B of Nvidia GB300 Racks It Cannot Yet Power, With About $3B More Arriving Monthly
items.dek: Power, not chips, is the binding constraint: purchased GPUs sit dark while capex runs near $220B.

analysis.happening: Business Insider reportedly found AWS staged ~$5B of GB300 racks in intermediary warehouses because some sites lack power to energize them, with ~$3B more per month projected in an internal email. Amazon's capex plan is cited near $220B this year.
analysis.now: Dark GPUs mean depreciation without revenue, an under-quoted risk to Nvidia backlog quality. Caveat: figures are from secondary coverage of the original, and Amazon reportedly disputes the framing.
analysis.future: Watch Amazon's Q3 call for capex and free-cash-flow language. Opportunity: power-ready sites, on-site generation, staging tooling.

items.headline: NYC's Asymptote Labs Raises a $5.5M Seed Led by Tower Research Ventures to Audit Coding Agents, Starting With a Free Open-Source Tool
items.dek: Beacon logs what Claude Code, Codex and Cursor actually do; the paid platform blocks risky actions.

analysis.happening: Asymptote Labs, founded by ex-Doppel engineers, raised a $5.5M seed led by Tower Research Ventures with Lytical, 1984 Ventures and South Park Commons. Open-source Beacon logs prompts, commands and file edits across 20+ agent tools; a paid platform adds blocking.
analysis.now: Open-source adoption first, enterprise control layer second is the emerging agent-security playbook. Caveat: valuation and customers are undisclosed, and the round predates this window slightly.
analysis.future: Watch Beacon's GitHub traction and whether Anthropic, OpenAI or Cursor ship native audit logs. A Japan-localized compliance layer is open.

items.headline: DeepSeek Open-Sources DeepInfer, the Production Inference Engine for V4.1-Flash, Under Apache 2.0 With Nvidia and Huawei Ascend Support
items.dek: Solo builders can now read how a frontier-class MoE model is really served, though the release is partial.

analysis.happening: DeepSeek released DeepInfer on Oct 20 under Apache 2.0, running on Nvidia SM100 GPUs and Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs; it supports only V4.1-Flash-1017. One aggregator reported 14,000+ GitHub stars within a day.
analysis.now: A useful reference for speculative decoding and structured-output kernels. Caveat: one report says KV-cache management, prefill/decode disaggregation and load balancing are omitted, so it is not a full serving stack; performance figures are self-reported.
analysis.future: Watch independent benchmarks, community ports to other models, and whether Ascend support makes non-Nvidia self-hosting practical outside China.

items.headline: METI Clears TSMC's Kumamoto Fab 2 for 3nm, but at Only 6,000 Wafers a Month and First Shipments in Dec 2028
items.dek: Japan gets its first 3nm logic fab at one-eighth of the 2024 plan's volume and about a year behind Arizona.

analysis.happening: On Oct 16 METI approved JASM's revised Fab 2 plan: 3nm logic at 6,000 wafers/month, down from 48,000 at 6-12nm. Reported subsidy cap falls from ¥732B to ¥645B. Commercial output targets Dec 2028; Fab 1 shifts to 22-28nm.
analysis.now: Gap: Japan finally hosts a leading-edge node, but tiny volume (reportedly EUV-tool limited) and no named customer. The ¥645B figure rests on one secondary source; check METI's release.
analysis.future: Watch the FY2027 budget top-up and customer names. Opening: packaging, materials and EUV-adjacent suppliers around Kumamoto.

items.headline: Japan's Government AI 'Gennai' Is Blind A/B-Testing Domestic LLMs Against Foreign Models, With a 2027 Procurement Call Due in November
items.dek: A captive public-sector market decides which Japanese models get paid contracts from April 2027.

analysis.happening: Five domestic models are on trial: tsuzumi 2, Sarashina3 mini, cotomi v3, Takane 32B and PLaMo 2.0 Prime, three on Sakura Cloud, in blind A/B tests Sep-Nov. A November call (300 questions, 35 criteria, one model per firm) feeds paid use from April 2027 across ~180,000 civil servants.
analysis.now: Gap: this anchor-customer lever has no US-lab equivalent in Japan, but the models are mostly 32B-class, so frontier parity is unproven. The foreign comparison model is unnamed and results are unpublished.
analysis.future: Partial results are expected around Jan 2027. Japanese-language agent and tool-use evaluation tooling is an explicit requirement.

items.headline: Yokohama's Tokyo Artisan Intelligence Raises ¥1.27B in a Series C First Close, Part Equity and Part Mizuho Loan, for Its Own Edge-AI Processor
items.dek: A small fabless startup tries to build a domestic edge-AI chip while Nvidia owns the datacenter.

analysis.happening: The first stage of its Series C mixes equity (Mitsui Sumitomo Insurance VC, Watakyu, Tokyo Keiki, ADT) with a Mizuho Bank loan. Funds go to the Manta Ray architecture and StingRay evaluation chip. It raised ¥1.11B in Series B in June 2025.
analysis.now: Gap: Japan's AI-chip startups are funded in single-digit billions of yen versus billions of dollars in the US. Industrial and rail backers point to infrastructure edge AI. Caveat: the equity/debt split is undisclosed and I found one 2026 source.
analysis.future: Watch final close size, a production-chip tape-out date and rail or factory customer commitments.

items.headline: Strip Out Sakana's ¥31B and Japan's H1 2026 Startup Funding Grew Just 2%; the Seed-to-Pre-A AI Median Is ¥160M, Barely Above All Sectors
items.dek: Money is concentrating in a few big rounds, while October's early AI deals are small vertical plays.

analysis.happening: H1 2026 funding was ¥377.9B (+12% YoY), about +2% excluding Sakana's ¥31B Series D. Rounds of ¥50B+ rose from 4 to 9 while smaller rounds fell 1%. AI seed-to-pre-A median is ¥160M versus ¥150M overall. October: The Phage ¥570M.
analysis.now: Gap: Japan has no AI premium at seed, unlike the US, so early AI-native competition in regulated verticals is thin. Caveat: data runs to July 22 and the median comes from a secondary blog.
analysis.future: Watch Q3 totals and any foreign funds entering the thin seed-to-A layer. Medical, health data and billing verticals look cheap to enter.
